6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability
9	
10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise
7	
8	/-!
9	# B-5 at the Abel chart: what the pointwise datum unfolds to, and what it costs
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduces `ChartsCoverLocally` — hence B-6 — to a
12	four-part datum at each point of each test.  That reduction is stated for an *arbitrary*
13	family of presheaf maps, so it says nothing about how hard the datum is at the family that
14	matters.  This file instantiates it at `abelSigmaChart` and computes the answer.
15	
16	## The computation, and the one thing it makes visible
17	
18	A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf C` over a **bare** test scheme `T` is by definition a *pair*
19	`⟨a, λ⟩` with `a : T ⟶ Spec k` and `λ` a degree-zero class on the slice object `Over.mk a`
20	(`Over.sigmaExtension`, `Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`).  And `(Over.mk a).left` is `T`
21	itself, definitionally.  So the big-site/slice crossing that looks like it needs a bridge does
22	not: the pointwise datum's `t : ↥T` *is* a point of the slice test, and `chartLocus` applies to
23	it with no transport.  `abelChartApp_eq` below records the crossing as an equation rather than
24	leaving it to unfold at a use site.
25	
26	What the computation *does* make visible is where the cost sits.  `abelSigmaChart`'s value at
27	`x : W ⟶ D.left` is `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv …)⟩`, so matching it against the
28	restriction of `⟨a, λ⟩` needs **both** components: the Σ-component is an equation between
29	morphisms to `Spec k`, and only then is there a class equation.  A producer that supplies the
30	class half alone has not supplied the datum — the Σ-component is what pins the chart point to
31	lie *over* the test, and it is free only because `W.ι ≫ a` is what `D.hom` must equal.
32	
33	## THE CORRECTION THIS FILE CARRIES, against this lane's own headline
34	
35	`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:40` says of its `chartLocusOpens`:
36	
37	> `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised — the `W` field costs zero, which is
38	> a real reduction of the datum from four fields to three
39	
40	**The second clause is false, and the roadmap `c9b` row repeats it** ("`W` needs nothing").
41	`chartLocusOpens` takes an argument `haff`, the affine-local openness of the locus at every
42	affine open of the test, and *nothing in the tree discharges it*:
43	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance.lean`) removed the
44	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis and passes `haff` straight through, as does
45	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it.  The affine case that would feed it is
46	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`), which is
47	itself conditional on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's *named residue*.
48	
49	**Update, same session** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`): that residue is now
50	*entirely witness-free*.  Its forward half already was (the trivial splitting), and its
51	converse `hconv` — the descent direction, open for three sessions — is discharged by plus-unit
52	injectivity.  So what `haff` ultimately costs is a `cechPicClass` base-change identity: no
53	witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, and nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
54	
55	So the honest accounting is: **`W` costs `haff`, which costs B-4's presentation residue.**  The
56	datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  What is
57	genuinely free is the type-level crossing above, and `chartLocusHaff` below is the residue
58	named so it cannot be lost again.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelChartApp_eq` — the Abel chart's value at a point of the divisor
63	  scheme, as an explicit `Sigma.mk`.  Both components, since the datum needs both.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartLocusAffineLocal` — the `haff` residue, named.  This is what
65	  `chartLocusOpens` silently costs.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens_of_affineLocal` — `chartLocusOpens` from it, so the
67	  dependency is explicit in the API rather than in an argument position.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation` — the residue **reduced to B-4's
69	  own named obligation**: a per-affine-piece `IsChartDatumPresentation` gives it.  This is the
70	  link that was asserted in `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring and never written.
71	-/
72	
73	set_option autoImplicit false
74	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
75	
76	universe u
77	
78	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
79	
80	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
81	
82	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
83	
84	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
85	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
86	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
87	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
88	
89	noncomputable section
90	
91	/-! ## The Abel chart's value, both components -/
92	
93	/-- **The Abel chart map evaluated at a point of the divisor scheme.**
94	
95	`abelSigmaChart` is `rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (chartValueTrans …)`, and
96	both factors act componentwise on the Σ-extension, so the value at `x : Y ⟶ D.left` is the
97	pair whose structure morphism is `x ≫ D.hom` and whose class is the chart value of the divisor
98	family `rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)`.
99	
100	Recorded as an equation because a coverage producer has to match this against a *given*
101	section, and the match is two equations rather than one: the Σ-components must agree before
102	the classes are even in the same type.  Leaving it to unfold at the use site is how the
103	Σ-component gets forgotten. -/
104	@[simp]
105	theorem abelChartApp_eq {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
106	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
108	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
109	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (x : Y ⟶ D.left) :
110	    (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y) x
111	      = ⟨x ≫ D.hom, ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom))
112	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)),
113	        chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩⟩ :=
114	  rfl
115	
116	/-! ## The `haff` residue, named
117	
118	`chartLocusOpens` takes the affine-local openness as an argument.  Naming it is not cosmetic:
119	an argument in a definition's signature is invisible to a census of open obligations, which is
120	how "the `W` field costs zero" survived into two roadmap rows. -/
121	
122	variable (C) in
123	/-- **The affine-local openness residue of `chartLocus`** — what `chartLocusOpens` costs.
124	
125	For a test `T` and a class `lam` on it, this says the chart locus is open over every affine
126	open piece of `T`.  It is exactly the `haff` argument of `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'`,
127	and it is the *only* remaining input to CHART-U(b) at a general test: the iso-invariance
128	hypothesis that used to sit beside it was discharged
129	(`isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds`), but this one was passed through, not proved.
130	
131	Named as a `Prop` so that it appears in searches for open obligations. -/
132	def ChartLocusAffineLocal (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
133	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : Prop :=
134	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
135	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
136	
137	variable (C) in
138	/-- `chartLocusOpens` with its cost made explicit in the API.
139	
140	Identical in content to `chartLocusOpens` — the point is that the dependency is now a named
141	`Prop` a reader can grep for, rather than an unnamed argument that reads as bookkeeping. -/
142	def chartLocusOpens' (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
143	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
144	    (haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam) : T.left.Opens :=
145	  chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff

147	@[simp]

8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-6: the local-surjectivity half of the `(f, hf)` handoff
10	
11	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) needs two things beyond the
12	charts: the `hf` certificate (C9b, reduced in `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`) and the
13	instance
14	
15	```
16	[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
17	```
18	
19	which is dat-b row B-6.  Three files carry that instance as a `variable`
20	(`JacobianDataCharts.lean:117`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183`,
21	`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131`) and **nothing anywhere produces one**.  This file supplies
22	the producer, in the form that DAT-B's coverage statement can actually feed.
23	
24	## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here
25	
26	Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
27	every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
28	`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.
29	
30	For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
31	proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
32	B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
33	mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
34	`Sigma.desc`.
35	
36	The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
37	by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
38	`ChartsCoverLocally` below.
39	
40	## The honest scope, stated up front
41	
42	`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
43	is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
44	this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
45	producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
46	none to check.
47	
48	## Main declarations
49	
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
51	  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
52	  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the
54	  instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective` — the degenerate sufficient
56	  condition (a chart that is surjective on points of every test already covers), recorded so
57	  the hypothesis is visibly *satisfiable* and not a disguised falsehood.
58	-/
59	
60	set_option autoImplicit false
61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
62	
63	universe u
64	
65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
71	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
72	
73	noncomputable section
74	
75	variable (C) in
76	/-- **The coverage hypothesis of DAT-B, stated per chart rather than on the coproduct.**
77	
78	For every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the maps into `T` along which `s`
79	becomes the value of *some* chart of the family form a Zariski covering sieve.
80	
81	This is dat-b row B-5 verbatim — "every `pic⁰` point is Zariski-locally a chart point" — with
82	one deliberate design choice: the sieve is described through the individual `f i`, so a
83	producer discharges it by exhibiting, for each point of `T`, one open neighbourhood and one
84	index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
85	that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/
86	def ChartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
87	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
88	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)),
89	    (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T
90	
91	/-- **B-6**: the coverage hypothesis gives the local-surjectivity instance that
92	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
93	
94	The proof is the bookkeeping the row's name hides: the image sieve of `Sigma.desc f` contains
95	the image sieve of every individual `f i` — because a `T'`-point of `X i` gives a `T'`-point
96	of the coproduct through `Sigma.ι` — hence contains their supremum, and a sieve containing a
97	covering sieve is covering.
98	
99	Note what is *not* needed: no compatibility between charts, and no injectivity.  `Sigma.desc`
100	imposes no coherence condition across indices (the observation `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`
101	makes for `hf`, here again for coverage), so a heterogeneous atlas is admissible for B-6 on
102	exactly the same footing as a homogeneous one. -/
103	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
104	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
105	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) :
106	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) where
107	  imageSieve_mem {T} s := by
108	    refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_ (h T s)
109	    refine iSup_le fun i => ?_
110	    rintro T' g ⟨t, ht⟩
111	    -- transport the witness along `Sigma.ι` and use `Sigma.ι_desc`
112	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι (fun j => yoneda.obj (X j)) i).app (op T') t, ?_⟩
113	    rw [← ht, ← NatTrans.comp_app_apply, Sigma.ι_desc f i]
114	
115	/-- **The hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed.**
116	
117	If one chart of the family is surjective on the points of every test, the coverage hypothesis
118	holds — its image sieve is already the maximal sieve.  This is the degenerate case (and not
119	the geometric situation: no single Abel chart is surjective on all tests), but it rules out
120	the failure mode where a `Prop`-valued hypothesis turns out to be unsatisfiable and the
121	"reduction" above is therefore vacuous.
122	
123	Compare the two-sided check in `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`: there the question was whether the
124	datum was too *weak*; here it is whether it is too *strong*. -/
125	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
126	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (i : ι)
127	    (hi : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective ((f i).app T)) :
128	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
129	  intro T s
130	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_
131	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.top_mem T)
132	  intro T' g _
133	  exact le_iSup (fun j => Presheaf.imageSieve (f j) s) i g (hi (op T') _)
134	
135	end
136	
137	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity
7	
8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/

59	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
60	
61	universe u

67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
68	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

71	noncomputable section
72	
73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
74	
75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
78	
79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
80	
81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
84	
85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88	
89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
101	
102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
103	
104	variable (C) in
105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
106	
107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
110	
111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
123	
124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
137	
138	variable (C) in
139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
140	
141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
186	
187	end

9	/-!
10	# DAT-B B-5: the coverage datum RE-SPELLED in the slice — and why that discharges nothing
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105` (`abelChartApp_eq`) records that the chart
13	application is a **pair**, and its header warns that a coverage producer must match *two*
14	equations rather than one — the Σ-components before the classes are even in the same type.
15	Two roadmap rows and the c9b thread price the coverage datum accordingly.
16	
17	**This file first claimed that price was avoidable.  It is not, and the retraction is the
18	content.**  The claim was: a producer working in the slice over `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1)`, rather
19	than handing over a bare `x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ D.left`, gets the Σ-equation as `Over.w` "for
20	free".  What is true is that `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D` **is by definition** the pair of an
21	`x` and a proof that `x ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1`: `(Over.homMk x hx).left = x` and
22	`Over.w (Over.homMk x hx) = hx` both hold by `rfl`, so the two hypotheses are interderivable
23	and a producer can do nothing here it could not do before.  Refuted by a fresh-context audit
24	(inbox `I-1021`); the durable lesson is `I-1024`.
25	
26	**The reusable error, since it is subtle.**  The non-vacuity check this file ran — `rfl` on
27	`x ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1` at unconstrained `x` **fails** — was read as licensing the discount.
28	It forbids it.  An equation that is not definitionally free does not become free by moving
29	into a binder's type; it merely stops appearing as a goal, which is what made the report
30	convincing.  `slice_iff_bare` below is the one-line probe that settles such a question, and it
31	is landed so the claim cannot be re-made here.
32	
33	## What this file is, honestly
34	
35	A **re-spelling** of the coverage datum, with the pair equation traded for one class equation
36	plus a richer input type carrying the other.  `datum_of_slice` is one half of an equivalence
37	(`bare_of_slice` is the other), so by the `I-0896` criterion no obligation was reduced.  It is
38	worth keeping only because the slice spelling is the shape a divisor-side producer would want
39	— every such producer here is stated over `overSpec k S`, so a route through them needs the
40	identification of `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1)` with `overSpec k Γ(Y, W)` at an affine `W`, and that
41	identification is against the slice form, not the bare one.  That seam is not written here.
42	
43	The class equation is untouched and is the whole of what remains: it asks that the chart value
44	of the divisor family named by `g` **is** the given class restricted.  Its cost is a divisor
45	family over a *neighbourhood* produced from data at a *point* — a spreading-out, measured
46	absent from the tree for this carrier by two independent censuses (every `DivFamZar` producer
47	takes its base ring or the affine-opens limit first; the only spreading lemmas,
48	`exists_supportTube` and its `Confine` instance, act on the support locus of an already-given
49	local-equation system, not on a class; mathlib's `spread_out_of_isGermInjective'` is about
50	morphism germs).
51	
52	**A second limit, and it is the sharper one.**  The two composites below are stated at the
53	**unrestricted** chart `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is all of `D.left`.
54	`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54` and `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` both hold that antecedent 1 is
55	*false* there (the fibres are linear systems `|D|`, so it is not a monomorphism), while the
56	atlas the tree intends, `mixedParamChart`, has source `(V i : Scheme)`.  So these endpoints
57	supply antecedent 2 at a family where antecedent 1 fails, and the two do not co-instantiate —
58	`I-0861`'s V-coupling defect, filed here as `I-1022`.  The site content of
59	`Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean` is family-generic and does apply to `mixedParamChart`; only
60	these instantiated composites are stranded.
61	
62	## Main declarations
63	
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.sigmaComponent_of_slice` — the Σ-component of a slice morphism, which is
65	  `Over.w`.  **Not a discharge**: see `slice_iff_bare`.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.slice_iff_bare` — **the refutation of this file's original claim**, in the
67	  kernel rather than in prose: a slice morphism over `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1)` is exactly a bare
68	  morphism together with the Σ-equation, both directions by `rfl`.
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.datum_of_slice` — the datum equation of `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal`
70	  from the class equation in the slice, and `bare_of_slice` its converse, so the pair is an
71	  equivalence and reduces nothing.
72	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_slice` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from per-point slice
73	  data over affine tests.
74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_of_slice` — antecedent 2, from the same.
75	-/

82	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

84	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

86	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
87	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
88	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
89	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
90	
91	noncomputable section
92	
93	/-! ## The Σ-component, discharged -/
94	
95	/-- **The Σ-component of a slice morphism is `Over.w`** — true, and *not* a discharge of the
96	coverage datum's Σ-equation.  Read it with `slice_iff_bare` immediately below, which is why. -/
97	theorem sigmaComponent_of_slice {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
98	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (W : Y.Opens)
99	    (g : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D) :
100	    g.left ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1 :=
101	  Over.w g
102	
103	/-- **A slice morphism IS a bare morphism plus the Σ-equation** — the refutation of this
104	file's original "the Σ-component is absorbed for free" claim, stated so it cannot be re-made.
105	
106	Both directions are `rfl`: `Over.homMk` bundles `(x, hx)` into `g` with `g.left = x`, and
107	`Over.w` projects it back out.  So working in the slice **moves** the Σ-equation into the input
108	type; it does not discharge it, and a producer owes exactly what it owed before.  What changes
109	is only that the equation stops appearing as a goal — which is why the original claim looked
110	measured.
111	
112	The general form of this check (inbox `I-1024`): when a file reports an obligation absorbed by
113	a richer input type, derive the new hypothesis from the old one.  One probe settles it. -/
114	theorem slice_iff_bare {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
115	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (W : Y.Opens) :
116	    Nonempty (Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D) ↔
117	      ∃ x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ D.left, x ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1 :=
118	  ⟨fun ⟨g⟩ => ⟨g.left, Over.w g⟩, fun ⟨x, hx⟩ => ⟨Over.homMk x hx⟩⟩
119	
120	/-! ## The reduction: one class equation is the whole datum -/
121	
122	/-- **THE DATUM FROM A SLICE MORPHISM PLUS ONE CLASS EQUATION.**
123	
124	The hypothesis `hcl` is the class equation in the slice over `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1)`: the chart
125	value of the divisor family that `g` names is the given class, restricted.  Given it, the full
126	pair equation that `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` consumes holds — the Σ-component is
127	`Over.w g` and the `Over.mkCongr` transport is handled by `Over.sigmaExtension_ext`.
128	
129	This is the discount `abelChartApp_eq`'s header asks a producer to pay and a producer of this
130	shape does not owe. -/
131	theorem datum_of_slice {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
132	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
133	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
134	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
135	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
136	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (W : Y.Opens)
137	    (g : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D)
138	    (hcl : (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (Over.mkCongr (Over.w g)).op
139	        ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
140	          (Over.homMk W.ι rfl : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ Over.mk s.1).op s.2)
141	      = ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (g.left ≫ D.hom))
142	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl)),
143	        chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩) :
144	    (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) g.left
145	      = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s := by
146	  rw [abelChartApp_eq]
147	  rw [show ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s)
148	      = ⟨W.ι ≫ s.1, (pic0TypeFunctor C).map
149	          (Over.homMk W.ι rfl : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ Over.mk s.1).op s.2⟩ from rfl]
150	  exact Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C) (Over.w g) hcl
151	
152	/-- **The converse of `datum_of_slice`**, so the pair is visibly an equivalence and this file
153	claims no reduction (the `I-0896` criterion).  From the datum equation the class equation is
154	read off by `Over.sigmaExtension_snd_eq`, the same one-liner with the projection replacing the
155	constructor. -/
156	theorem bare_of_slice {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
157	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
158	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
159	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
160	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
161	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (W : Y.Opens)
162	    (g : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D)
163	    (hdatum : (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) g.left
164	      = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
165	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (Over.mkCongr (Over.w g)).op
166	        ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
167	          (Over.homMk W.ι rfl : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ Over.mk s.1).op s.2)
168	      = ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (g.left ≫ D.hom))
169	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl)),
170	        chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩ :=
171	  Over.sigmaExtension_snd_eq (pic0TypeFunctor C) (Over.w g) hdatum
172	
173	/-! ## Through to antecedent 2
174	
175	The two composites, so the discount lands at the seam rather than in mid-air.  Both are
176	stated for the ONE-CHART family `fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChart …`: the slice reduction is about
177	the chart application, which does not see the index, and heterogeneity is orthogonal
178	(`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`). -/
179	
180	variable (C π n) in
181	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` from per-point slice data over affine tests.**
182	
183	The hypothesis is the coverage obligation in its cheapest measured form: over an affine test
184	only (`Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean`), a slice morphism rather than a bare morphism (so
185	the Σ-component is `Over.w`), and one class equation.  Nothing else stands between it and the
186	sieve condition. -/
187	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_slice {ι : Type u} [Nonempty ι] {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
188	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
189	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
190	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
191	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
192	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
193	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (g : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D),
194	        (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (Over.mkCongr (Over.w g)).op
195	            ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
196	              (Over.homMk W.ι rfl : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ Over.mk s.1).op s.2)
197	          = ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (g.left ≫ D.hom))
198	              (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl)),
199	            chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩) :
200	    ChartsCoverLocally C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) := by
201	  refine chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal C _ fun Y _ s y => ?_
202	  obtain ⟨W, hyW, g, hcl⟩ := h Y s y
203	  exact ⟨W, hyW, Classical.arbitrary ι, g.left,
204	    datum_of_slice rep m Z hdeg Y s W g hcl⟩
205	
206	variable (C π n) in
207	/-- **Antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, from slice data over affine tests.**
208	
209	The composite with B-6 (`isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`).  This is the honest endpoint of the
210	reduction: the instance the DAT-glue seam consumes, from the cheapest form of the coverage
211	datum the tree can currently state.
212	
213	**The class equation is still open**, and it is the whole of what is left here.  Its cost is a
214	divisor family over a *neighbourhood* produced from data at a *point* — a spreading-out, absent
215	from the tree for this carrier. -/
216	theorem isLocallySurjective_of_slice {ι : Type u} [Nonempty ι] {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
217	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
218	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
219	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
220	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
221	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
222	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (g : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D),
223	        (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (Over.mkCongr (Over.w g)).op
224	            ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
225	              (Over.homMk W.ι rfl : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ Over.mk s.1).op s.2)
226	          = ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (g.left ≫ D.hom))
227	              (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl)),
228	            chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩) :
229	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
230	      (Sigma.desc (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg)) :=
231	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc _ (chartsCoverLocally_of_slice C π n rep m Z hdeg h)
232	
233	end

8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: the coverage obligation is Zariski-local in the test, so AFFINE tests suffice
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduced `ChartsCoverLocally` — and with it
12	antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — to pointwise data at **every test scheme
13	`T`**.  That is where the reduction chain stops, and the quantifier it stops at is the
14	problem this file addresses.
15	
16	**Every divisor-side producer in this project is indexed by a RING, not by a scheme.**
17	`DivFamZar C S π n` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235`) is a quotient of local-equation
18	systems over an algebra `S`; `divFamZar C π n T` at a general test
19	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean:187`) is the affine-opens *limit* of those, and the
20	comparison `divFamZarAffineEquiv` (:300) collapses it to `DivFamZar` only on an affine
21	test.  Likewise every producer of a certified family, of an effective witness
22	(`DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:147`), and every classifier
23	(`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar`, :217) is stated over a ring or a field.  So a coverage
24	lane facing "for every scheme `T`" has to cross the affine-to-general gap **before** it can
25	use any of that machinery, and nothing said it was allowed to skip it.
26	
27	It is allowed to skip it, and that is this file's content.
28	
29	## Why locality in the test is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
30	
31	The naive argument — "sieves are local, so restrict to an affine cover" — is not available
32	as stated, because `ChartsCoverLocally` is a statement about the sieve on `T` itself, and
33	the pointwise hypothesis quantifies over points of `T`.  Three things have to be checked,
34	and each is where the argument could fail:
35	
36	* **the class must restrict.**  The datum at a point `t` of an affine piece `Y` is about a
37	  section over an open of `Y`, while the obligation at `t : ↥T` is about an open of `T`.
38	  Composing `W.ι ≫ 𝒰.f j` gives a map into `T` but not an *open of* `T`, so the transport
39	  cannot be done at the level of `T.Opens` — it has to be done at the level of the sieve,
40	  where an arbitrary morphism is allowed;
41	* **the sieve must be transitive.**  Membership of `⨆ i, imageSieve (f i) s` in the
42	  topology on `T` is deduced from membership of its *pullbacks* along the cover maps, which
43	  is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive` plus `Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve` — the latter is
44	  what says the pullback of an image sieve is the image sieve of the restricted section,
45	  i.e. that the obligation at `Y` is about `s|_Y` and nothing else;
46	* **the pullback must commute with the supremum.**  `Sieve.pullback` is a left adjoint on
47	  sieves, so it preserves `iSup`; without that the per-piece obligations would be about a
48	  different sieve than the one the pullback of the target names.
49	
50	None of the three mentions `pic⁰`, a chart, or a divisor.  That is the point: the
51	affine-to-general passage for antecedent 2 is a fact about the site, and mixing it with the
52	geometry is what made it look like part of the geometry's price.
53	
54	## What this does and does not buy
55	
56	It buys the quantifier, and only the quantifier.  `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` below
57	asks for the pointwise datum **only over affine schemes**, and produces
58	`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test; `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` composes that
59	with B-6.  So a producer may now assume its test is `Spec S` and reach for
60	`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, `DivisorFamilyFieldSurj`, `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` and the rest
61	of the ring-indexed machinery directly.
62	
63	It does **not** produce the datum at an affine test.  That is B-5's geometry and it remains
64	open; per `Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` and the `dat-b` row the residue there is
65	the class-side question, and per `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` the range containment `hV` is
66	a further separate obligation.  What changes is that the residue is now stated where the
67	tree's producers live.
68	
69	**On the converse, corrected.**  An earlier version of this paragraph said
70	`affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` makes the affine and general forms "equivalent", and cited
71	that as discharging the `reduction-needs-its-converse` safeguard.  It does not: that
72	declaration is `rfl`-equal to `pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally`, its `[IsAffine Y]` binder is
73	never used, and the direction it certifies is the *free* one — general pointwise data gives the
74	affine data by `fun Y _ s y => h Y s y`.  So the affine form is a genuine **weakening** of the
75	general one, which is exactly why `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` is worth having; the
76	honest certificate is that theorem, not a no-op converse (audit `I-1023`).  The converse is
77	kept only as the affine-test instance of the pointwise extraction, which is what it is.
78	
79	**On the atlas, and this is the sharper limit.**  Nothing here pins `V`.  The statements below
80	take an arbitrary family `f`, which is what makes the site content reusable — but a consumer
81	must supply coverage at the *same* `V` at which antecedent 1 was certified, and `ajcr-p1`
82	measured both ends of that range to be bad: `hf` is free at `V = ⊥` (`isChartUniv_bot`, with a
83	construction that never mentions the Abel chart), while `V = ⊤` returns the unrestricted
84	certificate that three headers call false.  So any workable `V` is a proper intermediate open,
85	CHART-U(b)'s openness is load-bearing, and the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` has **no measured
86	inhabitant at any `V`** (`I-1012`).  Two bad endpoints are two refutations, not a non-vacuity
87	check.
88	
89	## Main declarations
90	
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine` — **the site fact**, with no
92	  presheaf and no chart: a sieve on `T` is covering as soon as its pullback along every map
93	  from an affine scheme in a cover of `T` is covering.
94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` — **the reduction**: pointwise
95	  coverage over affine tests only gives `ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` — the composite with B-6, i.e.
97	  the instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, from affine-test data alone.
98	* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the converse, so the affine form
99	  is not a strengthening.
100	-/

107	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
108	
109	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
110	
111	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
112	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
113	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
114	
115	noncomputable section
116	
117	/-! ## The site fact -/
118	
119	/-- **A sieve is covering as soon as it is covering after pullback to affine pieces.**
120	
121	Stated for an arbitrary sieve on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses.  The
122	cover is `Scheme.affineCover`, whose members are affine by
123	`Scheme.isAffine_affineCover`, and the deduction is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive`
124	against the presieve the cover generates.
125	
126	This is the step the coverage chain was missing: it says the Zariski-local-surjectivity
127	obligation may be discharged one affine piece of the test at a time. -/
128	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine {T : Scheme.{u}} (S : Sieve T)
129	    (h : ∀ (j : T.affineCover.I₀), S.pullback (T.affineCover.f j) ∈
130	      Scheme.zariskiTopology (T.affineCover.X j)) :
131	    S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
132	  have hcov : (Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows T.affineCover.X T.affineCover.f))
133	      ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T :=
134	    Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr ⟨T.affineCover, Sieve.le_generate _⟩
135	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.transitive hcov S ?_
136	  rintro Y g ⟨V, a, b, ⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
137	  rw [Sieve.pullback_comp]
138	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology.pullback_stable a (h j)
139	
140	/-! ## The reduction -/
141	
142	variable (C) in
143	/-- **THE AFFINE-TEST REDUCTION**: pointwise coverage over affine tests gives
144	`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
145	
146	The hypothesis is `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`'s, with `[IsAffine Y]` added and
147	nothing else changed.  So a coverage producer may assume its test is affine — hence, through
148	`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, that its divisor data lives over a *ring*, which is where every
149	producer in this project is stated. -/
150	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
151	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
152	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
153	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
154	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
155	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
156	  intro T s
157	  refine mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine _ fun j => ?_
158	  -- the pullback of the supremum is the supremum of the pullbacks, and each is the image
159	  -- sieve of the RESTRICTED section — so the obligation at the affine piece is exactly the
160	  -- affine instance of the hypothesis
161	  have hpb : (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s).pullback (T.affineCover.f j)
162	      = ⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i)
163	          ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (T.affineCover.f j).op s) := by
164	    -- `Sieve.pullback` preserves `iSup` (it is a left adjoint), and per index it turns the
165	    -- image sieve of `s` into that of `s` restricted along the cover map
166	    simp only [← Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve]
167	    ext Y g
168	    simp only [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply, Sieve.pullback_apply]
169	    aesop
170	  rw [hpb]
171	  -- the piece is affine (`Scheme.isAffine_affineCover`), so the hypothesis applies AT IT — note
172	  -- `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` cannot be cited here, since it quantifies over all tests
173	  -- and would demand the datum at the non-affine ones too; the site bridge is what is reused
174	  choose W hW i x hx using h (T.affineCover.X j)
175	    ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (T.affineCover.f j).op s)
176	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun y => ⟨x y, hx y⟩
177	
178	variable (C) in
179	/-- **B-5 over affine tests ⟹ B-6**: the local-surjectivity instance
180	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, from affine-test coverage data alone. -/
181	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
182	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
183	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
184	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
185	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
186	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
187	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal C f h)
188	
189	/-! ## The converse -/
190	
191	variable (C) in
192	/-- **The affine form is not a strengthening**: `ChartsCoverLocally` gives back, over each
193	affine test, a cover on whose members some chart hits the section.
194	
195	Read the carrier honestly, exactly as `pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` does: the sieve
196	condition returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with open-immersion maps, not by opens of
197	the test, so the converse produces a cover map where the hypothesis consumed an opens
198	inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — that the affine-only hypothesis is available, not
199	chosen for provability — a cover map is exactly as good. -/
200	theorem affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
201	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
202	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y]
203	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) :
204	    ∃ (𝒰 : Y.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
205	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
206	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s :=
207	  pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally C f h Y s
208	
209	end

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageFibre

/-!
# B-5 assembly: from the fibre step to `chartLocus` membership over a GENERAL test

`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean` runs `w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–6 at a splitting field and
produces `IsSplitWitness` of a twisted class over `overSpec k L`.  The coverage theorem
(§1.2's `pic0_chartLocus_cover`) is a statement about a point `t` of a **general test** `T`:

```
∃ c : ChartIndex C, t ∈ chartLocus c lam
```

This file closes the gap between the two, which is one substitution and one collapse:

* the fibre class at `t` is `picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam`, a class over the field
  `κ(t)` — so the fibre step applies at `K := κ(t)` with no change;
* `chartLocus` is *defined* as the split-witness predicate of the twisted class at that field
  point, and the twist commutes with restriction (`picEtMap_chartTwist`), so
  "`IsSplitWitness` of the twisted fibre class" **is** membership, by `Iff.rfl`.

The second point is worth stating as a lemma rather than inlining: `chartTwist` is applied to
`lam` over `T` and then restricted, whereas the fibre step produces the twist of the
*restricted* class over `κ(t)`.  Those are equal, but not syntactically — `picEtMap_chartTwist`
is the law, and `mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre` is the resulting membership rule.

## What remains of B-5 after this file

**Twice corrected; read the DEFECT section for the full history.**  This header first said the
only residues were the two per-fibre choices; a degree probe added a third (step 6's feedback);
and on 2026-07-28 that third was **removed again** — not by discharging it but by showing
coverage needs no drop, hence no feedback (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`).  Step 2 is
likewise landed now (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`).

The two per-fibre choices, which are residues *of the route through this file*:

* **step 3, the twist exponent `m`.**  Chosen against the fibre's OWN DAT-0a bound `b_L`.  No
  uniform `m₀` exists (§0.2.2, I-0204), so this is a genuine `∃ m` produced inside the
  coverage proof, at the fibre.
* **step 5's oracle instantiation.**  `Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`'s density keystone at
  `P :=` the base-changed `K_s`-points, whose `residueDeg = 1` comes from
  `rationalPointBaseChange_snd`.

Both are `L`-level statements; neither is `divRep`- or certificate-gated.  Everything between
them and `chartLocus` membership is now landed.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre` — the membership rule: a split
  witness for the twisted *fibre* class puts `t` in `chartLocus`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_drop` — **the B-5 assembly**: the fibre step's
  hypotheses, at `K := κ(t)`, give `t ∈ chartLocus`.
-/

/-! ## The membership rule -/

variable (C) in
/-- **A split witness for the twisted FIBRE class puts the point in `chartLocus`.**

`chartLocus` twists over `T` and then restricts to `κ(t)`; the fibre step produces the twist of
the already-restricted class.  `picEtMap_chartTwist` says those agree, and
`chartTwist_eq_mul_thetaFamily_chartTwistClass` puts both in the collapsed spelling the fibre
step uses.

Stated as a named rule because the two sides differ syntactically and a lane that inlines the
substitution will meet the mismatch inside a proof about degrees, where it is least welcome. -/
theorem mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre (m : ℕ)
    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
    (h : IsSplitWitness C
      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam
        * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) (overSpec k (Over.testPointField t)))) :
    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam := by
  rw [mem_chartLocus_iff, picEtMap_chartTwist,
    chartTwist_eq_mul_thetaFamily_chartTwistClass]
  exact h

**The arithmetic.** `hW₀` puts `W₀` in the class `M₀ · (twist class at Z)`.  For a degree-zero

  `deg W₀ = m·d₁ − deg_k Z`,

and `hdeg` demands `deg W₀ = g + e`.  Under the chart-index constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g`

**What that means.** The pack is *satisfiable* — it instantiates, and at `e = 0` the theorem is
the true statement "a witness of degree `g` gives `chartLocus` membership".  It is not vacuous.
But `w4-datb` §1.2's argument runs the drop at a **different stage** from the chart index:

* the drop runs on `λ·θᵐ` — i.e. at `Z := 0`, where `chartTwistClass C m 0 = θᵐ` and the degree

* its **output** `Σ` is then the chart index's `Z`, at which the twisted class has degree `g`.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartRationalGraph
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeSeedUnivAssembleKappa
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.CoverageDrop

/-!
# B-5, the fibre step: the greedy drop RUN at the splitting field, as a `chartLocus` witness

**Title corrected (issue I-0615): this file is steps 4 and 5, not "4–6".**  Step 6 — feeding the
drop's output `Σ` back as the chart index — is NOT here and is not discharged anywhere; see the
DEFECT section of `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageTest.lean`, which explains why the drop stage and the
index stage carry different `Z`.  The original "4–6" wording is what that retraction corrects.

`w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–5 happen entirely on the curve over the splitting field `L`.  This file
runs them and hands the result to `Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean`'s introduction rule, so
that what comes out is membership of `chartLocus`.

## The statement, and what is a hypothesis rather than a construction

`exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop` takes:

* the presentation of the *twisted* fibre class over `L` by a Čech class `M`
  (`hM` — supplied at step 1 by `picEtAffineEquiv_map_chartTwistFactor_eq_unit`);
* a divisor `W₀` in that class with vanishing `H¹` and degree `g + e`
  (`hdeg`/`h1` — supplied at step 4: the class's degree is computed by
  `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegree.lean`, and the vanishing comes from the fibre's OWN
  vanishing bound, which is where step 3's per-fibre `m` is spent);
* the admissible point oracle at `L` (`hdense`/`hPcl`/`hPdeg` — supplied at step 5 by
  `Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`'s density keystone at the base-changed `K_s`-points).

and produces an `S ≥ 0` of degree `e`, supported in the oracle, with `h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`,
`h¹ = 0`, together with `IsSplitWitness` at the twisted class.

**What is deliberately a hypothesis:** the *existence* of `W₀` of the right degree with
`h¹ = 0`.  That is DAT-0a at the fibre field, and per `w4-datb` §0.2.2 (the I-0204 discipline)
its bound `b_L` is a **per-fibre** constant that provably does not transport from `k` — so it
must be chosen at `L`, inside the coverage proof, against `L`'s own instance.  Threading it as
a hypothesis here keeps that choice visible instead of burying it: a caller who cannot produce
`W₀` has not yet done step 3.

**Why the `h⁰ = 1` conclusion is carried even though `IsSplitWitness` does not ask for it:**
the witness predicate asks only for vanishing `H¹` (documented at `IsSplitWitness`; the
worksheets' "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`" is stronger than what the tree's
predicates state).  But `h⁰ = 1` is what DAT-C's normalization and GAP-2's uniqueness need, and
it is free here — the drop produces it.  Dropping it from the conclusion would force a later
lane to re-run the induction.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop` — **the fibre step of B-5**: the greedy drop
  at `L`, packaged as `IsSplitWitness` of the twisted class plus the `h⁰ = 1` normalization.
-/

    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
    [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
    (g e : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀
      = M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (g : ℤ) + e)
    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1))
    (P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
    (hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
      (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1) :
    IsSplitWitness C (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) (overSpec k K))
      ∧ ∃ S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (e : ℤ) ∧
        (∀ (x : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
          (hx : x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)),
          coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
        Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) = 1 ∧
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
          ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) 1) := by
  refine ⟨isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1, ?_⟩
  -- the χ-value at the fibre field, transported from `k` (genus is base-field invariant)
  -- The instance pack of `BaseChangeInstances` is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling
  -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`, not to the `relCurve` alias, so `chi_relCurve_baseField`'s
  -- `relCurve`-spelled binders do not synthesise without these three re-keyings.
  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
  have hχL : Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (g : ℤ) :=
    chi_relCurve_baseField C L g hχ
  exact exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one (K := L) g hχL P hdense hPcl hPdeg W₀ e hdeg h1

end

/-!
# COVERAGE NEEDS NO DROP, NO ORACLE, AND NO STEP 6

A retraction of this lane's own account of B-5, and it removes a residue rather than adding one.

`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageTest.lean`'s DEFECT section establishes — correctly — that the
`w4-datb` §1.2 argument as written runs the greedy drop at `Z := 0` and feeds the drop's
**output** `Σ` back as the chart index's `Z`, so that the two stages carry different `Z`, and
that this feedback ("step 6") is not discharged anywhere.  It records step 6 as one of B-5's
open residues.

**Step 6 is not a residue, because coverage does not need the drop at all.**

## Why: read what `chartLocus` actually asks for

`IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) — and its own docstring says this at length, under
"A convention this predicate INHERITS" — asks for a divisor `W` in the presenting class with
`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, and asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  Effectivity and the
degree normalisation are what the *chart map's injectivity* needs (GAP-2, `h⁰ = 1`), not what
*membership of the locus* needs.

The drop (`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean`) exists to manufacture exactly those two extra
properties: it takes a degree-`g+e` witness with `h¹ = 0` and produces an effective `S` with
`h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`.  For membership, that work is thrown away — `mem_chartLocus_of_drop` returns
the `IsSplitWitness` half from `hW₀`/`h1` alone, and its own proof shows this: the split witness
comes from `isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1`, in which the drop,
the oracle `P`, `hdense`, `hPcl`, `hPdeg`, `g`, `e`, `hχ` and `hdeg` **do not appear**.

So the feedback of step 6 was an artefact of routing coverage through the drop.  Cut the drop
and there is one `Z` again — the chart index's — and nothing to feed back.

## What coverage then needs, in full

Exactly one input beyond the landed splitting: a divisor of the twisted fibre class over the
splitting field with vanishing `H¹`.  That is DAT-0a at the fibre field, and it is genuinely
per-fibre (I-0204, `w4-datb` §0.2.2): no uniform `m₀` exists, so the exponent `m` must be chosen
against `L`'s own threshold `b_L`.

**CORRECTED 2026-07-30 in its second sentence** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageThreshold.lean`,
inbox `I-1329`).  The *threshold* is not per-fibre.  I-0204 says the per-field ledger
**constants** do not transport — true — but the vanishing bound induced at `L` is base-field
data: `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness` (`RiemannRoch/WindowFieldTransport.lean:87`) is
π-free, `windowN C L hπ g` is a witness at every `L`, and `deg_windowN = M·δ` with
`windowM_choice`/`windowδ` computed at `k`.  So `M·δ + g` is **one threshold for every
splitting field**.

**TWO CORRECTIONS TO THAT CORRECTION, both the same day** (audit + author reproduction, inbox
`I-1349`/`I-1350`), so read the paragraph above only for its central point:

* the sentence that stood here — "DAT-0a itself cannot be instantiated at `L`, there is no
  `relCurve C L ⟶ P1 L` in this tree" — is **FALSE**.  `exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1`
  (`Curve/MapToP1.lean:126`) produces one for `baseChangeBundle C L` via the instances in
  `Curve/BaseChangeInstances.lean`, so DAT-0a *is* available at `L`;
* the uniform threshold is **not new Lean** either: `subsingleton_h1_of_windowA_le_deg`
  (`Picard/DivSchemeSeedUnivFibre.lean:259`, landed 2026-07-19) is the same fact at a *smaller*
  bound (`windowA_choice ≤ windowM_choice`).  Cite that, not
  `subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound`.

What survives is only the correction to the *"per-fibre"* reading itself, which was the point.
Also unaffected: the retraction below, `hb_forces_h0_eq_one`, and the whole `b = g` discussion,
since both `M·δ + g` and `a·δ + g` exceed `g` for `δ ≥ 1`.

**RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (I-0660).**  This paragraph continued: `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound`
"takes `b_L` in exactly the shape `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`
produces it, and *derives* the `m` — so what remains of step 3 is instantiating DAT-0a at the
base-changed curve, not choosing anything."  That is FALSE.  At a chart index legal at parameter
`n` the `hdeg` hypothesis **forces `b = n`**, and at `n = g` the resulting `hb` is a statement
that is false in general — see the retraction note on
`mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` itself and `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` for the
three machine-checked statements that replace it.  The theorem below is sound; only this account
of what remains was wrong.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1` — **coverage, drop-free**: a splitting plus a
  vanishing witness in the twisted class gives `t ∈ chartLocus`.  No `g`, no `e`, no `χ`, no

* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` — the same with the witness *produced*

* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` — the `∃ m` form: the coverage
  statement `w4-datb` §1.2 targets, at a fixed chart-index shape.
-/

    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
    (b : ℤ)
    (hb : ∀ D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
      b ≤ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) 1))
    (hdeg : classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
      (chartTwistClass C m Z)) = b) :
    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam := by
  -- The instance pack of `BaseChangeInstances` is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling
  -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`, not to the `relCurve` alias, so the `relCurve`-spelled
  -- binders of `exists_picClass_eq` / `classDeg_picClass` do not synthesise without these
  -- re-keyings (the same pack `Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean:130` needs).  The `hdeg`/`M₀`
  -- binders are therefore stated in the PRODUCT spelling, so that the statement itself needs
  -- no re-keying — `relCurveMap C k L` is `(C ◁ overSpecMap (ofId k L)).left`
  -- (`relCurveMap_eq_overSpecMap_ofId`), which is also the spelling
  -- `classDeg_presenting_twist` delivers.
  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq L
    (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
  refine mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1 C lam t m Z M₀ hM₀ W hW (hb W ?_)
  rw [show Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W
      = classDeg L (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W) from (classDeg_picClass L W).symm,
    hW, hdeg]

variable (C) in
/-- **The coverage statement in `∃`-form**, i.e. `w4-datb` §1.2's target shape at a fixed chart
index: at a point whose splitting is known and whose twisted class hits the threshold, there is
a chart the point belongs to.

Trivial given the previous theorem; recorded because it is the shape the DAT-B B-6 packaging
(`IsLocallySurjective`) consumes, and because keeping it separate makes visible that the only
`∃` coverage still owes is over the *index*, not over any witness or drop. -/
theorem exists_mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T)
    (t : T.left) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    -- The `classDeg L` of `hdeg` is applied to a `relCurve`-spelled class, and the
    -- `BaseChangeInstances` pack is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`,
    -- so these three do not synthesise in the STATEMENT (a `haveI` in the proof is too late).
    -- They are not new assumptions: `instIsIntegralBaseChange`,
    -- `instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange` and `instQuasiCompactBaseChange` discharge
    -- them at every instantiation, and the proof below re-derives the rest of the pack.
    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
    (b : ℤ)
    (hb : ∀ D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
      b ≤ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) 1))
    (hdeg : classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
      (chartTwistClass C m Z)) = b) :
    ∃ m' : ℕ, ∃ Z' : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor, t ∈ chartLocus C m' Z' lam :=
  ⟨m, Z, mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound C lam t m Z M₀ hM₀ b hb hdeg⟩

end

end AlgebraicGeometry
